title: Glasgow Bridge
own_dating_reasoning: Rooftop panel URIE / ARTIST / PHOTOGRAPHER on the building across Jamaica St: John Urie, photographer, 83 Jamaica St, listed 1870-71 to 1887-88, elsewhere from 1891-92. PAISLEY'S on the white building numbered 96: Paisley at 80 to 96 Jamaica St from 1883-84 (72 Jamaica St 1880-81 to 1882-83). Fascia THE ST MUNGO VINTNERS' CO.: listed 1881-82 to 1895-96. A Clutha ferry is in view (Cluthas ran 1884-1903, per record). Horse traffic, no overhead tram wires. A painted sign can outlive its tenant, so the upper bound is soft.
viewpoint: From the south bank, west of Glasgow Bridge (the 1878 railway bridge is at the left edge, in the foreground), looking north across Glasgow Bridge to the foot of Jamaica Street; the Paisley's corner (NW corner of Jamaica St x Broomielaw) left of centre, the NE corner of Jamaica St x Clyde St at centre, the Custom House at right.
legible_signs: PAISLEY'S (top of white building) | CLOTHIERS | PAISLEY'S (shop fascia) | 96 (rooftop) | URIE / ARTIST / PHOTOGRAPHER (rooftop panel, east side of Jamaica St) | THE ST MUNGO VINTNERS' CO[MPANY] (fascia, partly legible)
licence_rights: Reproduced with the permission of Glasgow City Council, Glasgow Museums (TheGlasgowStory)
visual_check: yes: 1000 px web copy, zoomed crops
notes: Earliest view of Paisley's found. The white building shows PAISLEY'S / CLOTHIERS / PAISLEY'S on a flat frontage (cf. H2), but seen from across the river. TheGlasgowStory's 'c 1900' is contradicted by the signs. Viewpoint corrected 15 Nov 2026: the railway bridge in the left foreground puts the camera west of Glasgow Bridge, not east. Valentine 287 J.V. (P30) was taken from the same spot at about the same date, but it is a different exposure (different traffic; a landing stage with a kiosk where P01 has a Clutha ferry).
